source_solver: gurobipy 13.0.3 (Gurobi 13.0.3, size-limited pip licence), original notebook code cells run unmodified (only the %pip line dropped and the image-display cell skipped) on 2026-10-02; the notebook's stored output (Gurobi 9.5.1) shows the same 437 rows, 1397 columns, 3541 nonzeros and optimal objective 4.008123940e+08
notes: Objective unique; procurement 354457744.76 + transport 46354649.24; 324391.38 units of food bought (six foods: Wheat, Oil, CSB, Milk, DSM, Maize meal). HiGHS, SCIP and CBC through PuLP reach 400812394.0027498 / 400812394.00274974 / 400812394.00310916, and the HiGHS solution equals Gurobi's to 4e-12. Min/max over the optimal face shows the total, procurement and transport cost and the food bought are unique, at the base and within 1e-5 relative over about 300 generated what-ifs; per-camp rations and per-supplier purchases are unique at the base but tied in some what-ifs, so they are reported, not scored. Reformulation: the original's nutrition rows are gurobipy ranged rows (min <= intake <= 2 * min), which Gurobi stores as an equality plus one range column each (77 RgR columns, hence 1397 columns although the notebook counts 1320 decision variables); the port writes the same equality and bounded range variable (nutrient_surplus), so all 437 rows, 1397 columns, 3541 nonzeros and 1080 nonzero objective coefficients match. The two numbers hard-coded in the notebook are parameters: max_nutrient_factor = 2 and max_purchase = 10000000. Data: the six CSVs of food_program/data (the folder has six, not seven), values copied verbatim; edge_costs.csv lists 84 node-level links (supplier/transit/camp nodes), which the notebook keys by city pair with the last row winning, giving 37 links (only Hama -> Jubb_al_Jarrah conflicts: 147.6 on the supplier rows, 148 on the transit rows; 148 is used); prices are the 'Mean' column of food_costs.csv, with the international price for the 160 supplier-food pairs without one. Left out because the model does not use them: road distance/duration, the node-level link labels, the transit-hub (TS) node rows and the monthly price history. Changed for robustness, identical on the published data: every city named by a supplier, camp or link gets a balance row (the original writes rows only for suppliers and camps, so a pure transit hub would let food appear for free; none exists in the data). The 72 flows on the zero-cost links from Daraa, Dayr_Az_Zor and Hassakeh to themselves net out of their balance row and appear only in the objective, as in the original; they are kept for the size but are not part of the flow measure.
